solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I fantasise about everything under the sun

definitions.text: I fantasise about everything under the sun
definitions.note: The clue speaks as the answer: 'I' am the daydreamer.

parts.note: reads as someone whose fantasies cover every subject there is
the setter means literally beneath the sun, in daylight: this dreamer does it by day

explanation.surface: A confession from someone whose imagination roams over absolutely everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything under the sun' reads as 'all topics'; cryptically, 'under the sun' means in daylight, so this fantasist dreams by day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydreamer fantasises while awake, in the daytime.

clue.text: Troubles making love lead to icy insults

indicators.note: the troubles word is made into something else by the swap

parts.note: to dog = to trouble or plague
love = O, the zero score in tennis; this is the letter swapped out

indicators.note: the lead of 'icy' is its first letter

parts.note: the lead (first letter) of icy, swapped in for the O

explanation.surface: Romance soured, with frosty put-downs now the only thing a couple exchanges.
explanation.walkthrough: Take DOGS and turn its love, O, into the I that leads 'icy': DOGS becomes DIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs are pointed remarks, small verbal insults.

clue.text: Chicken on top of stove turns golden

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of stove, placed below in this down answer

explanation.surface: A cooking note: the chicken on the hob is browning nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' is the cowardly adjective, not the bird on the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To yellow is to take on a golden colour, as old paper or leaves do.

clue.text: I will show you the first of these things

definitions.text: I will show you the first of these things

parts.note: reads as a speaker offering a demonstration
the setter means the clue's opening letter itself: read as a number, that single stroke is 1, the first of a set of symbols

explanation.surface: Someone offering to demonstrate the first item in a series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the letter I, which is 1, the first Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The numerals I, II, III... are written with letters, and I is the first of them.

clue.text: During fall, Altman shot around one uni, then another

definitions.note: An adjective; 'during fall' works as in 'autumnal (during-fall) weather'.

indicators.note: a shot item is ruined and ready to be rearranged
the rearranged ALTMAN goes around the two Us

explanation.surface: Film-making news: Robert Altman shooting in autumn around a couple of universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' fits the film director Altman so neatly that it hides its job; 'fall' is the American word for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumnal means of or during autumn, which Americans call the fall.

clue.text: After knight leaves, tidy up and put away food

definitions.note: EATEN is the participle: food 'put away' has been eaten.

parts.note: to neaten is to tidy up
N = knight in chess notation; removed from NEATEN

explanation.surface: Once the knight has gone, the servants clear up and put the leftovers away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' reads as storing food in the larder; here it means eating it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: putting food away is informal for eating it, and the participle describes the food once consumed.

clue.text: Toothy type conservative Gordon Bennett backed

indicators.note: backed = turned back to front

parts.note: both are exclamations of surprise; turned back it gives ROC

explanation.surface: A toothy Tory politician getting the support of someone called Gordon Bennett.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon Bennett!' is a British exclamation of astonishment, like 'Cor!'; 'backed' reads as supported, not reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc (crocodile) is a creature famous for its teeth.

clue.text: Buy the farm if interior of study gets fitted out

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it; opened up as REA...D
'buy the farm' is American slang for dying

explanation.surface: A farmhouse purchase that goes ahead if the study is kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buy the farm' looks like a property deal; it is slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something readied has been prepared, fitted out for use.

clue.text: Can we sleep after seismic event and landslide?

indicators.note: after an earthquake everything is shaken up, so the letters are too

explanation.surface: Anxious residents wondering whether they can rest after an earthquake and a landslip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landslide' sits beside 'seismic event' as a natural disaster; it is the election kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide victory wins everything, a clean sweep.

clue.text: Maine journal rebuffed one with feet of clay

indicators.note: re-buffed, pushed back, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A Maine newspaper turning away a flawed figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet of clay' suggests a hidden flaw; the golem of Jewish legend is literally made of clay.
explanation.definitionFit: A golem is a figure moulded from clay and brought to life.

clue.text: Tickle flipping relations into the small hours?

parts.note: til late = until late at night

explanation.surface: Some cheeky relations tickle each other until the early morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family but means sexual relations, IT; 'flipping' also works as a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to tickle, literally or by arousing interest.

clue.text: Lag delights in messing around authorities

indicators.note: the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: An old prisoner happily winds up the prison bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: A lag is a convict, so the authorities look like the prison warders, but they are the fodder's own anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading lights are prominent figures, authorities in their field.

clue.text: Garnish on a rotten main wants spicing up

indicators.note: the letters need livening up, mixing

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic: the garnish on a poor main course can't hide that it needs more flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' looks like the anagram indicator but is part of the fodder; the indicator is 'wants spicing up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garnish is decoration, ornamentation, added to food or anything else.

clue.text: In league A, field a fit Batty

indicators.note: batty = crazy, so the letters go mad

explanation.surface: A cricket instruction: in the top division, put out a fit side to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'League', 'field' and 'Batty' all point at cricket or football, and 'Batty' looks like a player's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Affiliated means officially connected, in league with.

clue.text: Duke you left by a river of reeds, perhaps

explanation.surface: A duke leaves someone beside a reed-lined river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman; 'put up your dukes' means raise your fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Fistular means hollow and tube-shaped, as reeds are.

clue.text: Light breeze over the eastern side of Barrow

parts.note: a breeze is a light wind

indicators.note: in an across entry the eastern (right-hand) side is the last letter

explanation.surface: A gentle breeze drifting across the east of Barrow, a Cumbrian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light breeze' reads as one phrase; 'Light' is the definition and only 'breeze' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An architectural sense: a light is any opening or pane that lets daylight into a building.

clue.text: Dynasty over at last, first parts of Cops on next

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next two words

parts.note: first letters of Cops and on
over at last, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: A TV schedule: the drama series Dynasty is finally over and the cop show comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a TV listing, with Dynasty and Cops as shows; the definition 'next' is the continuity announcer's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming up means next, as in a broadcaster's 'coming up after the break'.

clue.text: One with busy people nursing ten beastly types

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close

parts.note: busy as a bee; opened up as BE...ES

explanation.surface: A carer among busy staff looking after ten unruly animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy people' are bees, not humans.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats, types of beast.

clue.text: Sovereign contrary agent hid in foreign capital

indicators.note: contrary = the other way round, so the result is turned back
to hide in something is to be concealed within it

parts.note: the Italian capital, foreign to a British solver; opened up as RO...ME
a rep = a representative, an agent

explanation.surface: A spy story: a king's double agent lying low in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' could be the gold coin; here it is the ruler, and 'contrary agent' teases the double agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the ruler of an empire is its supreme monarch, the highest kind of sovereign.

clue.text: Inferior E, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an adjective: poor in quality, second-rate
an E is a mark near the bottom of an exam scale, given by example

explanation.walkthrough: E is a low grade in a school or exam marking scale, so 'E, perhaps' describes the answer by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-grade means inferior in quality; an E is literally a low grade.

clue.text: When you want a lot of unopened porridge

indicators.note: MANY without its opening letter

parts.note: a lot of = MANY, which unopened drops its M
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, time

explanation.surface: A breakfast offer: have as much porridge as you like, whenever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' sits there as breakfast; in British slang doing porridge means serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the informal adverb for at whatever moment suits the person asking.

clue.text: Wild claim about power, skill and relentlessness

indicators.note: wild = uncontrolled, so CLAIM's letters are scrambled

parts.note: CLAIM rearranged, opened up as IM...LAC

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of their strength, talent and never giving up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a boastful list of virtues; the last one, 'relentlessness', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Implacability is the quality of being impossible to appease, relentless.

clue.text: Excellent work secures Magnus's first mate in Spain

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast
Magnus's first means the first letter of that name

parts.note: A1 = excellent, the 1 written as I; opened up as A...I

explanation.surface: A chess report: Magnus Carlsen's brilliant play delivers mate in a Spanish tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like checkmate from the world champion Magnus Carlsen; it is the friend sense, in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign-language definition: the Spanish word for friend, and mate is British for friend.

clue.text: Does dope in America finally graduate classes?

indicators.note: the final letters of the next two words

parts.note: last letters of graduate and classes

explanation.surface: A question about drug-taking at American college graduation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb of doing; with 'dope' it means takes drugs, which is what 'uses' means.
explanation.definitionFit: To use is slang for taking drugs, so 'does dope' is 'uses'.

clue.text: Object, having to take ill-considered punishment?

parts.note: an object is a thing; opened up as TH...ING

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at having to accept a hasty, badly judged penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest; it is the noun, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a severe beating given as a penalty.

clue.text: Those first in lines of songs on the radio

indicators.note: heard over the airwaves, so what counts is the sound

explanation.surface: Opening lines of songs being played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' reads as lyrics; it means lines of succession, which heirs are first in.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs stand first in line to inherit a title or estate.

clue.text: One heading to bed on board craft on delta

definitions.text: One heading to bed on board

parts.note: Delta = D in the NATO alphabet
a craft is an art or skill

explanation.surface: A passenger going to their bunk aboard a vessel on a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bed' is a scoring segment of a dartboard, such as the treble bed, and a dart is thrown at it; 'craft' looks like a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart flies to a bed (double or treble ring) on the dartboard.

clue.text: Tenor kidnapped by Brahms and Liszt? Rotters!

parts.note: both are composers; opened up as COMPOS...ERS

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at two great composers abducting a tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotters' reads as an insult; composters are things that make waste rot. 'Brahms and Liszt' is also rhyming slang for drunk, a second red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Composters rot garden waste down, so they are literally rotters.
